summary: Ryosei Fukuda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (earning a doctorate in literature in 1993). He became a professor at Taisho University in 1973, emeritus professor in 2007, and guest professor at Shuchiin University in 2012.

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1971 to 1975. He served as a professor at Hanazono University around 1991 and worked as a researcher at the Research Institute of Soto Studies.

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, later serving as professor, dean of the faculty of literature, and emeritus professor (1990–1994) at Taisho University.

Ryosho Nakamura is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura and earned a doctorate from Rissho University in 1977. He served as a professor at Kagoshima International University from approximately 1965 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He held multiple positions there, including assistant, professor (from 1964), dean, museum director, and president (2009), as well as professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology and studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1998) and at the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Otani University, where he later taught from around 1934 to 1974, and was an attested professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University in 1976.
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Waseda University between around 1946 and 1950, later serving there as an emeritus professor from approximately 1988 to 2010.

Ryoshun Okubo is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Waseda University. He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University around 2000, and is attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Ryosuke Furui is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007. He holds a post at the University of Tokyo, where he became a professor in 2020.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies researcher who pursued doctoral studies at Toyo University (attested 2015). In 2015, he was attested as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University and as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Shibuya was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his studies at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.
Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard Business School from around 1974 to 1976. He worked in banking and corporate sectors before becoming the leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii held posts with the JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).
Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2010) and remained affiliated with the university as of 2020.

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He spent his career at Rissho University as a lecturer (1960–1966), associate professor (1966–1975), professor (1975–2002), and president (1992–1998).

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. His appointments include teaching at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026), serving as a researcher at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (2014), and lecturing at Nishogakusha University (2013).

Ryuichi Abe is a Buddhist studies and Japanese religions scholar who studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia universities under scholars including Ryosei Fukuda. He taught at Columbia University before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard around 2006.

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as a professor and emeritus professor at Tohoku University, and as head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
